result.title: SEIS: Self-Evolving Inference Systems
result.summary: Inference systems determine how fast and how cheaply language models can be served, so making them faster has direct practical value. However, prior work focuses mostly on optimizing certain parts such as kernels or memory within the large system. In this work, we take a holistic approach and apply agentic self-evolution to optimize the whole system end-to-end. Our SEIS (Self-Evolving Inference Systems) autonomously optimizes the entire mini-sglang engine without human intervention through iterative sessions with inherited experiences and code changes. Serving Qwen3-0.6B on H100, the resulting engine reaches 3.27X the throughput of the original mini-sglang implementation and beats SOTA engines like vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, and SGLang in the single-request workload. The correctness of the optimized inference engine by SEIS is tested in terms of numerical difference and downstream accuracy on math and long-context retrieval tasks. The code and session histories show that the speedup comes from redesigning the whole engine and that building on earlier sessions beats independent attempts. These results suggest that agentic self-evolution can optimize a complex system end-to-end. The evaluation also has to evolve with the engine, and letting agents evolve it is a natural next step.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作提出 SEIS，用智能体自演化在无人工干预下迭代优化整个 mini-sglang 推理引擎，在 H100 上服务 Qwen3-0.6B 达到原实现 3.27 倍吞吐，并检验数值与下游任务正确性。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线无直接关联，但其「会话经验继承、跨尝试累积改造」的自演化搜索形式，可能为 latent 推理中轨迹训练、贡献分配与计算成本权衡的问题表述提供类比线索，需核查是否可迁移。
